answer: Each agent may join freely, but voting weight grows only with time-locked stake, and rewards accrue after a challenge period in which peers can expose duplicated identities or collusive transfers. Splitting one account into a hundred does not multiply the stake: it divides the same capital, while locking it prevents the attacker from using it elsewhere and risks slashing if fraud is proven. A prism, yarrow, and raven can each be pseudonyms, but none is a cheap extra vote.
